actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

facts.text: The Iudex environment is registered as SoulsGymIudex-v0 with max_episode_steps=3000 and nondeterministic=True
The Iudex observation is a Dict of 15 members: phase, player HP/SP and max HP/SP, boss HP and max HP, player/boss/camera poses, player/boss animations and durations, and lock_on
The Iudex action space is a Discrete space over the game's action table
The game action table maps 0-7 to walking, 8-15 to rolling, 16 and 17 to light and heavy attacks, 18 to parry and 19 to no action
SoulsEnv.step_size is 0.1 seconds between each step
SoulsEnv.step returns (observation, reward, terminated, False, info) and raises ResetNeeded when called after the episode terminated
The episode terminates when the player HP or the boss HP reaches zero
The Iudex reward is boss damage over boss max HP plus the player HP change over player max HP, with a +-0.1 terminal bonus and a small distance-to-centre shaping term
IudexEnv.reset accepts seed and options but does not use them, and it sets the player and boss to their fixed start poses
The README states that the environments are nondeterministic and cannot provide reproducible results by setting RNG seeds
The README requires the latest Dark Souls III running, on Windows or on Linux under Proton/Wine
SoulsEnv constructs a GameInput, a GameWindow and a game interface, and refuses to initialize when the player is not loaded into the game
SoulsEnv.close resumes the game, restores the altered game properties and kills the player to force a reload
SoulsEnv.render is a no-op because the game window must already be open

determinism.notes: this package's fake lays out an episode from the reset/seed value, so one seed repeats its trajectory; upstream SoulsGym cannot control the game's randomness (soulsenv.py:211-227) and IudexEnv.reset ignores seed and options (iudex.py:193-224), so the claim covers the fake only

gaps: analytic F0 model: HP, poses, actions and ticks advance directly; there is no physics, collision, contact, actuator, sensor or noise model, and no game memory is read or written
the real environment requires a running Dark Souls III on Windows or Linux under Proton/Wine and drives the game through its memory, input and window managers; the fake was not compared with a game
observations are Python lists of placeholder values; the real observation is numpy arrays built from the game's HP, poses and animation tables
seeded determinism is a property of the fake only: the game's reset ignores seed and options, and the README says RNG seeds cannot make SoulsGym reproducible
the real reset teleports, reloads and enters the fog gate through game input; the fake resets its internal state synchronously
no rendering (SoulsEnv.render is a no-op) and close only marks the fake closed; the real close kills the player and reloads the game
the episode is truncated at the registration's 3000-step limit, which gymnasium.make applies as a TimeLimit wrapper; the fake reports truncation itself

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the fake keeps its state and makes no native stop call
